posts.body: Agents leave because their broker isn't actually there. You close a deal and nobody knows. You hit a problem and you're solving it alone at midnight. You want to grow and there's no plan, no support, no one pushing you forward. Here's what they're really looking for instead. 1. A leader who shows up. Not just quarterly. Not just when something breaks. Someone who knows what you're working on and genuinely cares if you win or lose. 2. Systems that actually work. Most brokers have nothing. You're inventing your process from scratch every deal. Better brokerages give you a playbook so you're not reinventing the wheel every month. 3. A culture where your split doesn't matter more than your growth. You can negotiate a commission all day. What you can't negotiate is whether your broker believes you're capable of bigger things. The right brokerage isn't about percentage points?

Agents leave because they're solo. No one knows what they're working on. No one helps when deals break. No one pushes them forward. They're looking for a leader who shows up. Systems that work. A culture that invests in growth over splits. That's what we're building here.

We're running more buyer and lease leads than we can handle right now. New construction in San Antonio and Austin mostly, plus out-of-state relocations. Warm leads but they need vetting and nurturing. Most aren't transaction ready. If this sounds like something you'd take on, send me a DM.

I walked into one of our agent's listing appointment with her last month. She was nervous. First big listing in a competitive neighborhood. I stayed quiet, let her lead it, asked one question at the end that she hadn't thought about yet. She nailed the listing.

After we left, she told me that moment changed something. Not because I closed it for her. Because I showed up and believed she could do it before she believed it herself.

That's the difference between working somewhere and working for someone who has your back. You stop doubting yourself because someone else already knows you're capable.

That's what we're building at Lifestyle Design Realty. Leaders don't recruit agents. They build believers. When you know your broker is actually invested in your growth, you show up differently.

Had a listing go sideways this week. Inspection came back with foundation issues the seller didn't disclose. Deal almost died right there.

1. The agent panicked and wanted to renegotiate everything. I told her to stop. We called the inspector back, got clarity on what was actually structural versus cosmetic. Turns out it was fixable and cheaper than everyone thought. The buyer stayed. Deal survived.

2. Most agents never make that second call. They assume the worst and kill momentum. One conversation changed the entire outcome.

3. This happens because agents operate alone. No one to sanity check the panic. No one to say "wait, let's think this through before we blow it up."

When you've got support, deals don't fall apart over miscommunication. You solve them.

We have more buyer and lease leads than we can actually work right now.

1. Mostly new construction in San Antonio and Austin, plus out-of-state relocations coming in. The leads are warm but they need real vetting and nurturing before they're transaction ready.

2. Most of these buyers aren't buying tomorrow. They're buying in three months or six months. If you're the kind of agent who knows how to work a lead that isn't hot yet and turn it into a closed deal down the road, we have inventory for you.

3. The catch is real. They need patience and a system. You can't treat them like a hot buyer and expect to close in two weeks. You need to nurture. You need to follow up. You need to stay in front of them until they're ready.

If this sounds like something you'd take on, send me a DM.

Motivation doesn't come from the market. It comes from knowing someone believes in you when you don't believe in yourself yet.

I've been grinding through slow seasons too. I know what it feels like when your pipeline is thin and the self-doubt creeps in. That's the moment most agents quit or jump to a new brokerage hoping the grass is greener. It never is. What changes everything is having a leader who tells you what you're capable of before you see it. Someone who doesn't just talk about support but actually shows up when deals get messy. When you know you're not alone in this, you stay consistent. You keep making calls. You keep prospecting. You bet on yourself because someone else already did.

If you want to talk about what we're building at Lifestyle Design Realty, send me a DM.
